disclosure: When on, your Workbench messages and authorized users' private messages are offered for Memory capture. Your Agent can also submit long-lived notes for best-effort capture without being asked, including preferences, corrections, decisions, and lasting facts about your machine or accounts found in files, forwarded or shared content, or other non-plain content.

Memory capture is bounded and process-local: raw messages are not queued durably, and temporary attachment copies are cleaned after use or at startup. Saturation, failure, shutdown, or restart may lose work; ambiguous provider outcomes are not replayed.

To build memories, message content is sent to the model endpoints configured above, and Search sends queries there too. These endpoints are separate from your Agent's models, and their providers handle the data under their own policies.

Avibe's local Memory store stays on this machine and includes best-effort native Processing Records with original submitted items, processing status, attempts, timestamps, scrubbed errors, and directly linked memories. Records can be incomplete or lost. Copies sent to model endpoints are outside this local store. Turning Memory off pauses it — it doesn't delete anything.

Delete Memory data deletes Avibe-managed Memory data for every user and project on this machine, including profiles, memories, native processing data, and temporary attachment copies. It can't take back content already sent to model endpoints or touch original chat histories.
Accounts on different platforms each have their own separate memory; they aren't linked.
